questions.q: What event actually triggered Overlook Medical Group's board-level mandate?
options: An internal audit found a security flaw
A competitor healthcare network suffered a public data breach, prompting the board to ask whether the same thing could happen at Overlook
Overlook's database already suffered an outage
A new regulation was passed requiring the change
questions.explain: The pressure came from outside — a competitor's breach in the news — which is why leadership, not just the DBA team, got involved.

questions.q: Which four deliverables did the board specifically ask for?
options: A new database schema, a new application, a new website, and a new logo
A tested DR plan, a real security/compliance posture, real automation, and infrastructure defined as code
A bigger budget, more staff, a new office, and a new vendor
A faster database, a cheaper database, a smaller database, and a backup database
questions.explain: Those four — DR, security/compliance, automation, and IaC — map directly onto Chapters 2 through 6 of this capstone.

questions.q: How does this capstone differ from the Beginner and Intermediate Azure Database Engineer capstones at Overlook?
options: It uses a completely different, unrelated company
It is purely theoretical with no real deliverables
It repeats the same backup and performance work already done
It is a board-mandated, production-grade build — IaC, security/compliance, HA/DR, and automation — rather than one person reacting to a single known problem
questions.explain: Beginner fixed backups and Intermediate fixed performance, each as a single person solving a single known issue. This capstone is leadership deciding tribal knowledge isn't an acceptable foundation anymore.

questions.q: What was the honest state of Overlook's DR readiness before this project, according to the lesson?
options: It had already passed a real disaster recovery test
No one actually knew whether the company would survive a real incident — the database had never been through a real DR test
It had a fully documented and tested DR runbook already
DR wasn't relevant because Overlook had no production database
questions.explain: The honest answer to the board's question was 'we don't know' — exactly the gap this capstone exists to close.

questions.q: Why does the lesson call Infrastructure as Code part of the mandate, rather than just a nice-to-have?
options: Because it makes deployments slower on purpose
Because it's required by Azure and can't be avoided
Because it lets the environment be reviewed before deployment and rebuilt identically later, instead of existing only as undocumented manual Portal clicks
Because it eliminates the need for any security controls
questions.explain: Click-ops infrastructure has no record of how it was built or whether it can be reproduced — IaC is what makes the environment reviewable and reproducible.
